[2] The world is in a transition, driven by rapidly evolving security and technological challenges, causing stresses in international order and transforming the global hierarchies

[3] The need to craft an appropriate response, aimed at shaping an international environment conducive to India’s development and security, is imperative

[4] India’s foreign and defence policies seek to provide a peaceful and enabling environment for achieving transformative national growth and development

[5] A complex and increasingly unpredictable interplay of regional and global developments characterize India’s security environment

[6] Guided by the principles of strategic autonomy and mutually beneficial cooperation, India continues to address the wide spectrum of conventional and non-conventional security challenges by pursuing constructive engagement with partner countries at the bilateral, regional and global levels

[7] Terrorism and radicalisation are the biggest threats to peace and security that the world is facing today

[8] India has reiterated, at a number of bilateral and multilateral platforms, its resolve to combat terrorism in all its forms and manifestations

[9] The global concerns regarding proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and their delivery systems, continue to pose serious threats to international security

[10] WMD terrorism will remain a potent threat as long as there are terrorists seeking to gain access to relevant materials and technologies for malicious purposes

[11] India has contributed actively, with partners, to the success of Nuclear Security Summit (NSS) process and continues to engage with partners in the Nuclear Security Contact Group

[163] Internal Security Environment 1.35 The overall internal security environment in the country is under control due to the continuous and unrelenting efforts of the Central and State Governments

[164] In our federal structure, the primary responsibility for ‘Public Order’ and ‘Policing’ rests with the State Governments

[165] However, the Central Government is steadfastly assisting the States in dealing with problems such as terrorism, militancy, insurgency and extremism

[166] The range of challenges to internal security in India, emanating from terrorism/insurgency, can be categorised into four broad theatres, namely (i) Terrorism in the hinterland, (ii) Crossborder terrorism in Jammu & Kashmir (J&K), (iii) Insurgency in North-East and (iv) Left Wing Extremism (LWE) in certain states

[167] As far as terror-related cases in the hinterland is concerned, the overall situation is under control

[168] No major terror attack took place in the hinterland of the country during the year

[169] In November 2018, a grenade attack took place in Adliwal Village, Amritsar which resulted in loss of 3 lives and injuries to 23 others

[170] No major terror attack took place in the first quarter of 2019 in the hinterland

[171] State-sponsored terrorism by Pakistan in J&K remains the foremost internal security challenge faced by the country

[172] During the period from January 1, 2018 to March 31, 2019, our security forces were able to neutralize 305 militants

[173] Several development initiatives like strengthening of infrastructure, education, health, high-end security equipment for J&K Police, etc., under Prime Minister Development Package, 2015 have been taken in the State of J&K

[174] The overall security situation in the North Eastern (NE) States improved substantially since

[175] The year 2018 witnessed the lowest number of insurgency incidents and civilian deaths since

[176] Compared to 2017, insurgency incidents have registered a decline of 18% in the year

[177] Similarly, there was 25% reduction in number of civilians and security forces personnel deaths in

[178] In the first three months of 2019, security situation has further improved in the region with the decline in insurgency incidents, civilian casualties, Security Forces (SF) casualties and kidnapping/abduction cases

[179] Compared to the peak of insurgency in the region in the last two decades since 1997, there has been phenomenal improvement in security situation in the region

[180] While there is almost no insurgency left in Tripura and Mizoram, there has been a marked improvement in security situation in other States of the region

[181] Pursuant to policy of talks/negotiations, various insurgent outfits have entered into Suspension of Operation (SOO) agreements and some of them have signed Memorandum of Settlements (MOS) and dissolved themselves

[182] As a result, a number of cadres of insurgent outfits have surrendered after laying down arms and joined the mainstream of society

[183] Sustained counter-insurgency operations are continuing against insurgents

[184] The declining trend of LWE violence which started in 2011, continued in 2018 as well

[185] In the last five years, there has been an unprecedented improvement in LWE scenario across the country

[186] The improved security situation is a result of resolute implementation of the multi-pronged strategy encompassing security measures, development measures, ensuring rights and entitlements of local communities etc

[187] Greater presence of security forces across LWE States and severe attribution on armed LWE cadres through arrests, surrenders, desertions and neutralization in operations have contributed to the reduction in violence

[188] Several developmental initiatives have been taken specifically for development of LWE-affected areas including focused schemes for development of roads, setting up of mobile towers, skill development and financial inclusion etc

[189] apart from the flagship schemes of Central Government in infrastructure, education, health, agriculture etc. Organisation and functions of Ministry of Defence Chapter 2 ORGANISATIONAL SET-UP AND FUNCTIONS 2.1 After Independence, Ministry of Defence was created under the charge of a Cabinet Minister and each Service was placed under its own Commander-in-Chief

[190] In 1955, the Commanders-in-Chief were renamed as the Chief of the Army Staff, the Chief of the Naval Staff and the Chief of the Air Staff

[191] In November 1962, the Department of Defence Production was set up to deal with research, development and production of defence equipment

[192] In November, 1965, the Department of Defence Supplies was created for planning and execution of schemes for import substitution of defence requirements

[193] These two Departments were later merged to form the Department of Defence Production and Supplies

[194] In 2004, the name of Department of Defence Production and Supplies was changed to Department of Defence Production

[195] In 1980, the Department of Defence Research and Development was created

[196] In 2004, the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare was set up

[197] The Defence Secretary functions as head of the Department of Defence and is additionally responsible for co-ordinating the activities of the four Departments in the Ministry

[198] THE MINISTRY AND ITS DEPARTMENTS The principal task of the Ministry is to frame policy directions on defence and security-related matters and communicate them for implementation to the Services Headquarters, Inter-Service Organisations, Production Establishments and Research and Development Organisations

[199] It is required to ensure effective implementation of the Government’s policy directions and the execution of approved programmes within the allocated resources

[200] The principal functions of the Departments are as follows: (i

[201] The Department of Defence deals with the Integrated Defence Staff (IDS) and three Services and various Inter-Service Organisations

[202] It is also responsible for the Defence Budget, establishment matters, defence policy, matters relating to Parliament, defence cooperation with foreign countries and co-ordination of all defence-related activities

[203] The Department of Defence Production is headed by a Secretary and deals with matters pertaining to defence production, indigenization of imported stores, equipment and spares, planning and control of departmental production units of the Ordnance Factory Board and Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs

[204] iii) The Department of Defence Research and Development is headed by a Secretary

[205] Its function is to advise the Government on scientific aspects of military equipment and logistics and the formulation of research, design and development plans for equipment required by the Services

[206] iv) The Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare is headed by a Secretary and deals with all resettlement, welfare and pensionary matters of Ex-Servicemen

[207] A list of subjects dealt with by various Departments and Finance Division of the Ministry of Defence is given in Appendix-I to this report

[208] Information regarding the Ministers in the Ministry of Defence, the Chiefs of Staff, the Secretaries in the Departments of the Ministry and the Secretary (Defence Finance)/Financial Advisor (Defence Services) who held positions during the period of this report is given in Appendix-II to this report

[209] HQ IDS was raised on October 1, 2001 based on the recommendations of Group of Ministers (GoM) on the Kargil Review Committee (KRC) report

[210] The HQ was raised under the command & control of Chairman Chiefs of Staff Committee (COSC) to foster jointness and synergy amongst the three Services

[211] Since its inception, this HQ has achieved considerable milestones in joint and integrated planning, coordination of intelligence, joint conduct of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Operations and prioritising/streamlining procurements

[212] Salient achievements of HQ IDS, during the ensuing year are enunciated in succeeding paragraphs

[213] Unified Commanders’ Conference – 2018: HQ IDS conducted the Unified Commanders’ Conference (UCC) at New Delhi on July

[214] The conference provided a platform for discussions at the apex level on all ‘Joint’ issues amongst the three Services

[215] The conference was attended by the Raksha Mantri, National Security Advisor, Service Chiefs and other Senior military and civil officials of the Ministry of Defence and Tri-Services Organisations/Institutions

[216] Combined Commanders’ Conference – 2018: HQ IDS conducted the Combined Commanders’ Conference - 2018 on September 28, 2018 at Air Force Station, Jodhpur

[217] The Conference was aimed to provide a platform for exchange of ideas at the apex level with a view to taking stock of the activities of the past year and to formulate a way ahead for the future

[218] Participation of Commander-in-Chiefs of the three Services ensured feedback from the field formations to the highest decision making body thereby facilitating formulation of a way ahead in a comprehensive manner

[219] Under the Chairmanship of the Prime Minister, the conference was attended by the National Security Advisor, Defence Secretary and Financial Advisor (Defence Services) from the Ministry in addition to the three Service Chiefs, Chief of Integrated Staff to Chairman COSC (CISC), Vice Chiefs and all Commander-in-Chiefs (C-in-Cs

[220] Turnover of Chief of Integrated Staff to Chairman COSC (CISC): Lt Gen PS Rajeshwar, AVSM, VSM took over as CISC on November

[221] The officer was Director General Perspective Planning, IHQ of MoD (Army) prior to his present assignment

[222] As CISC, he is coordinating various important Tri-Services Operational, Training, Planning & Administrative issues

[223] New Raisings: Three new agencies viz Armed Forces Special Operations Division, Defence Cyber Agency and Defence Space Agency are being raised under Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff with the issuance of Government Sanction Letters from the Ministry of Defence

[224] The new agencies with its mandate and charters are designed to further embolden the idea of jointness and integration amongst the three Services achieving common national goal

[225] Joint Special Forces Training Camp: Joint Special Forces Training Camp is conducted annually under the aegis of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff with a view to furthering integration between the Services in the field of Special Operations

[226] This year the camp was conducted in March 2018 at Bagdogra

[227] Inauguration of National War Memorial: National War Memorial at ‘C’ Hexagon of India Gate was inaugurated and dedicated to the Armed Forces on February 25, 2019 by Prime Minister to commemorate the valour, sacrifice and selfless service of the Indian Armed Forces

[228] The entire project was steered by HQ IDS

[229] Armed Forces Veterans’ Day: The 3rd Armed Forces Veterans’ Day was held on January 14, 2019 as a mark of respect and commitment towards our Veterans

[230] It was celebrated at Delhi, Shillong, Patiala, Bikaner, Alwar, Kota, Dehradun, Meerut, Mumbai, Port Blair, Guwahati, Nagpur, Trivandrum and all major stations

[231] The Armed Forces Veterans’ Day is an outreach programme to interact with Veterans and to apprise them of the measures taken by the Services HQ and Ministry of Defence on matters concerning their pension and welfare on the occasion

[232] Chief of Integrated Staff to Chairman COSC along with one senior officer from each Service also laid a wreath at Amar Jawan Jyoti, along with Veterans of the three Services

[233] Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Activities 2.15 Kerala Floods: Kerala state received incessant rainfall for a period of two weeks from August 7, 2018 onwards

[234] The heavy rainfall created unprecedented flood situation worst in last 100 years, affecting 13 districts in the state

[235] The gates of 35 dams in the state had to be opened, exacerbating the floods situation in Central Kerala

[236] Idukki, Kochi, Ernakulam and Pathanamthitta were the worst affected districts

[237] INCP was activated during the crisis period

[238] HQIDS acted as Point of Contact for coordination of rescue/relief effort on behalf of Armed Forces

[239] Op SAMUDRA MAITRI (Indonesia floods): Sulawesi province in Indonesia was hit by an earthquake and Tsunami on September

[240] Palu in Central Sulawesi was most severely affected by the twin tragedy

[241] On October 1, 2018, decision was taken to extend humanitarian aid to Indonesia

[242] ARMED FORCES TRIBUNAL (AFT

[243] The Government has established Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) for the adjudication of complaints and dispute regarding service matters and appeals arising out of verdicts of the Court Martial of the Members of the three Services (Army, Navy and Air Force) to provide speedy justice to the members of the Armed Forces

[244] At present Armed Forces Tribunals have been functioning at Delhi (Principal Bench) and at Regional Benches at Chennai, Jaipur, Lucknow, Chandigarh, Kolkata, Kochi, Guwahati, Mumbai, Jabalpur and Srinagar are functional

[245] BORDER ROADS ORGANISATION (BRO) 2.19 Border Roads Organisation (BRO) is a road construction organization to meet the requirements of the Armed Forces

[246] Starting operations in May 1960 with two projects, it has now grown to 18 projects

[247] Nine BRO projects are located in North West India (4 in J.&K., 2 in Himachal Pradesh, 2 in Uttarakhand and 1 in Rajasthan), 8 BRO projects are located in North Eastern India (1 in Sikkim, 4 in Arunachal Pradesh, 1 in Nagaland, 1 in Mizoram and 1 in Tripura) and 1 in Bhutan

[248] BRO has earned a reputation of being the only road construction agency to construct and maintain roads in difficult, isolated and inhospitable terrain in inclement weather conditions

[249] BRO has constructed approximately 53600 km of roads, 633 major permanent bridges of 57600 metre length and 19 Airfields

[250] At present, BRO is undertaking construction/upgradation work of 19415 km roads and maintaining 7992 km roads, seven airfields besides snow clearance of 4219 km roads to ensure connectivity of border regions with rest of the country

[251] Major achievement by BRO (a) Completion of Theng Tunnel: To negotiate frequent landslides at km 86 on road Gangtok-Chungthang, a Horseshoe shaped tunnel of NHDL specification having length 578 meter has been completed

[252] This tunnel has been dedicated to nation by Raksha Rajya Mantri on June

[253] b) Se La Tunnel: Prime Minister has laid the foundation stone of Se La Tunnel on February 9, 2019 and construction work through EPC contract has been awarded. (c) Akhnoor – Poonch Road: The Akhnoor – Poonch Road is planned to be upgraded to National Highway Double lane (NHDL) specs with paved shoulders

[254] The proposed upgradation also includes four tunnels and bypass that will ensure all weather connectivity and result in a reduction of about 34 km in the overall distance

[255] Foundation stone for this upgradation works was laid by the Prime Minister on February

[256] d) Rohtang Tunnel: After breakthrough of Rohtang Tunnel in Himachal Pradesh was achieved, the concrete lining works have been progressed at an accelerated pace

[257] Civil works are expected to be completed by third quarter of Financial Year

[258] e) Completion of ICBR: Government has identified 3812 km roads for development along Indo-China border

[259] Out of this, road length for 3418 km have been entrusted to BRO, with overall completed length 2300 km and connected length 3205 km. (f) Highest Motorable Road in Ladakh

[260] Project Himank has constructed the World’s highest motorable road in Ladakh region of Jammu and Kashmir, passing Umingla Top at an altitude of 19300 feet

[261] This strategically important road of length 86 km, connects border villages (China border) Chismle and Demchok to the mainland of Leh and will play important role in safe movement of troops to Indo-China border

[262] g) Adoption of EPC mode in BRO: Adoption of Engineering Procurement Contract (EPC) mode of execution has been approved by Ministry of Defence on August

[263] Accordingly, all works costing more than 100 crore has been planned to execute through EPC mode

[264] At present, 40 works have been planned to be outsourced through EPC mode

[265] As of date 33 contracts for preparation of DPRs have been accepted and 7 cases are in tendering process

[266] The following civil works have been awarded through EPC mode: (i) Chardham Yatra Projects: Contract for construction of 83.215 km on Chardham Yatra Projects on Road Rishikesh-Joshimath-Mana, Rishikesh-Dharasu and Dharasu-Gangotri Roads in Uttarakhand for 724.19 crore has been awarded to various firms

[267] Se La Tunnel: Contract for construction of two tunnels of length 0.475 km and 1.79 km at Sela Pass along with the approach Roads of length 9.775 km on Balipara-Charduar-Tawang Road in Arunachal Pradesh for 647.22 crore has been concluded on February

[268] Upgradation: Contract for construction Road Balipara-Charduar-Tawang stretch between km 70 to 88 km in Arunachal Pradesh from CG-9 to NHDL specifications for 170 crore has been concluded

[281] While constantly reviewing its operational preparedness/postures to meet the perceived security challenges, the Indian Army (IA) is committed to the defence of the country from external and internal threats across the entire spectrum of warfare

[282] Also, in times of disaster/natural calamities, the Indian Army is in the forefront, providing aid and succour to the affected people

[283] The situation in J&K has remained volatile

[284] Our deployment along the Line of Control (LoC) and hinterland along with accretional forces has facilitated the Security Forces to maintain momentum of operations against terrorists

[285] In the hinterland, the districts of Pulwama, Shopian, Anantnag and Kulgam remained the hub of terror related activities

[286] Along the LC, areas South of Pir Panjal Ranges remained violent due to frequent Ceasefire Violations while the infiltration attempts from North of Pir Panjal Ranges have continued as hithertofore

[287] Ceasefire Violations (CFV): The ceasefire along the Actual Ground Position Line (AGPL), LC and International Border (IB) Sectors in J&K was generally held

[288] In the year 2016 post Uri terrorist attack, the tempo of CFVs increased considerably and has remained constant this year too

[289] There were 228 CFVs along the LC in 2016, 860 CFVs in 2017 and 1629 CFVs in

[290] Appropriate and effective retaliation, wherever required, was carried out to the CFVs initiated by Pakistan

[291] The incidents of CFVs are taken up through the established mechanisms of hotlines, flag meetings and Directorate General of Military Operation talks between both countries

[292] Infiltration: Active training and aiding of terrorists continue from across the border to infiltrate through the LC

[293] The efficacy of our Counter Infiltration grid has resulted in heavy attrition on infiltrating terrorists and lowering of successful infiltration across the LC

[294] In 2018, Army eliminated 15 infiltration bids resulting in 35 terrorists killed

[295] In 2017, the Army had eliminated 33 infiltration bids resulting in 59 terrorists killed

[296] Situation in Hinterland 3.5 Security Forces achieved remarkable success in the year

[297] Operations were conducted in excellent synergy with J&K Police and CRPF

[298] Terrorist leadership and Over-Ground Workers (OGWs) were targeted effectively

[299] terrorists have been eliminated by the Security Forces in 2018 in J&K. Suspension of Offensive Operation (SoOO) declared by the Government with effect from May 17 to June 16, 2018 provided an opportunity to the populace for peaceful celebration of the holy month of Ramzan

[300] The terrorists, however, disregarded the initiative and used the opportunity to coerce the population, neutralize sympathizers of security forces, strengthen their network and increase terror incidents

[301] Tempo was, however, restored after the resumption of operations

[302] Significant dent has been made to the terrorist organisations by inflicting heavy attrition and eliminating its leadership

[303] Attempts of the terrorist groups to revive militancy in North Kashmir was thwarted by maintaining sustained pressure

[304] As a result the recruitment was largely restricted to the districts of South Kashmir

[305] Terrorists on their part tried to maintain higher levels of violence

[306] As compared to 131 Terrorist Initiated Incidents (TIIs) in 2017, 318 were reported in

[307] This was done with a view to expanding their writ in the society by terrorizing the population and subverting Government institutions

[308] SPOs, SF personnel on leave and innocent civilians including women were brutally killed

[309] The incidents, however, were largely restricted to South Kashmir and by the end of the year, due to sustained pressure, recruitment declined

[310] Attempts of Tanzeem to boost their number also received setbacks as 71% of terrorists were eliminated within months of picking up arms

[311] As a result, due to sustained pressure, the local recruitment which had seen a spurt in activity during 2016, declined by year-end

[312] Overall security situation remained under control

[313] Amarnath Yatra, Urban Local Bodies and Panchayat elections were conducted without any security related incidents

[314] Situation Along the Line of Control (LC) 3.10 Cease Fire Violations (CFVs): Sustained pressure was maintained on the LC and violations by Pak Army were appropriately retaliated

[315] Pak Army sought DGMO talks on May 29, 2018 during which implementation of Ceasefire Understanding of 2003 was proposed

[316] The proposal was accepted by our DGMO

[317] During talks held on June 13, 2018, our concerns including infiltration of terrorists from Pakistan were conveyed

[318] Pakistan also sought a Brigade Commanders Level Flag Meeting on June

[319] During the Flag meeting, our concerns of infiltration were reiterated and measures to ensure controlled movement of civilians close to the LC were proposed

[320] The CFVs reduced post DGMOS talk

[321] CFVs, however, increased in the run-up to the Surgical Strike Anniversary celebrations

[322] The CFVs in September, October and November have been largely reported in Poonch and Naushehra Sector in South of Pir Panjal Range

[323] Caliber escalation reduced significantly post the May 29, 2018 talks

[324] Probing attempts continued from across and stand-off firing on our posts occurred in regular intervals

[325] A befitting retaliation was done to Pak in Sunderbani Sector on November

[326] In response, Pakistan sought DGMO talks on November 15, 2018 and Brigade Commander Level Flag Meeting on November

[327] Our commitment to maintain peace along the LC was conveyed to Pak

[328] At the same time, it was emphasized that infringement of our Red Lines would invite massive punitive retaliation

[329] The Army has assiduously combated terrorism in the State through people-friendly operations based on precise intelligence to break their nexus, with a larger aim of helping the civil administration in establishing its writ and bring about peace and stability in Jammu and Kashmir

[330] The endeavor would be to further strengthen the counter-infiltration grid and maintain sustained pressure on Pakistan Army along the Line of Control by well-calibrated punitive retaliation to any act of misadventure

[331] Human Rights in J&K Indian Army continues to maintain its stellar Human Rights record in J&K and assiduously investigates cases of alleged violations received from National Human Rights Commission

[332] In 2018, Indian Army received 15 allegations from the NHRC of which six investigations have been completed and all of them have been found false

[333] Balance allegations are currently under investigation

[334] Pakistan, with renewed vigour in 2018, orchestrated an international campaign on Kashmir through its sponsored proxies by trying to project law and order maintenance actions as trumped-up human rights cases of excess use of force

[335] Pakistan’s effort to portray Kashmir issue has received a fillip, following the publication of two international reports by the Office of the United Nations Human Rights Commission and the British Parliament's ‘All-Party Coordination Committee’

[336] Indian Army is proactively engaging with MEA and MHA to counter propaganda both at international and national fora

[337] NORTH EAST

[338] The security situation in the North Eastern States has improved on all parameters with only sporadic incidents of violence over the year

[339] Inputs reveal that insurgent groups are facing acute administration and financial crunch due to relentless operations by Security Forces and have been forced to form umbrella organisation to maintain their capability for orchestrating violent activities

[340] Concurrently, the tribal and ethnic divide, fuelled by the issue of illegal immigrants, has gained momentum and is likely to have a pan-North East impact

[341] Proactive operations by Security Forces continued and in 2018, 620 terrorists were neutralized along with recovery of 619 weapons

[342] Assam: The security situation in the State remained largely peaceful and under control

[343] Calibrated, synergised and coordinated operations by security forces significantly reduced the operational space of insurgent groups

[344] NDFB (S) and ULFA (I) have been marginalised leading to demoralisation and disenchantment amongst its cadres

[345] Insurgent groups are facing acute financial crunch and have resorted to extortion and sporadic acts of violence to prove their relevance

[346] National Citizen Register (NRC) update and Amendment to Citizenship Bill remain challenging issues and are likely to adversely impact law and order situation in the State

[347] Nagaland: Security situation in the State has improved considerably since

[348] State elections were held peacefully in February 2018 and resulted in a record turnout

[349] In September 2017, the Naga Peace Process reached an important juncture with the signing of Framework Agreement with the NNPGs (conglomerate of six Naga insurgent groups

[350] Talks between the Government and the Naga groups are underway to ensure early finalization of the peace process

[351] The impeachment of Khango Konyak from NSCN(K) resulted in a split in the group based on Indian and Myanmar Nagas

[352] The Khango Konyak led faction has shown inclination of joining the peace talks and the ceasefire agreement

[353] The developments have ensured that the Naga Peace Talks have become more inclusive and are progressing towards the solution for achieving lasting peace in the State

[354] Manipur: Security situation in the State continues to remain fragile and it remains the most disturbed State in the North East region

[355] Majority of the violence has been perpetrated by valley-based groups as they accounted for approximately 60% of the violence in Manipur

[356] Inter-tribal rivalry and insider-outsider divide were prominently visible during

[357] With the passing of Manipur People’s Protection Bill by Manipur Assembly, there are increased demands for implementation of Inner Line Permit in the State

[358] Politics of Blockades and Bandhs continued to prevail and led to increasing fissures amongst the three major communities namely Meiteis-Nagas-Kukis

[359] There is also increased activity of Civil Society Organisations seeking clarification on the content of the Framework Agreement and who have been voicing concerns over maintaining territorial integrity of Manipur in light of the NSCN(IM)’s claim for Nagalim

[360] Arunachal Pradesh: Security situation in Arunachal Pradesh has been gradually improving in terms of reduction in violent incidents, lower civilian casualties and increasing number of apprehension of terrorists

[361] Synergised operations by Special Forces have reduced the operational space of insurgents

[362] Apart from the complete districts of Longding, Tirap and Changlang, areas falling under the jurisdiction of eight Police Stations along the Assam border have been declared as ‘Disturbed Area’ for six months beyond September

[363] Earlier, areas under 11 Police Stations were declared as ‘Disturbed Area’

[364] Longding, Tirap and Changlang districts of the State are affected by the presence of various Naga insurgent groups which continue with their revival attempts

[365] Since the area shares its borders with Assam and Myanmar it is frequented by cadres of NDFB(S) and ULFA (I) for shelter/transit

[366] There are attempts by joint groups under United National Liberation Front of West South East Asia (UNLFW SEA) to showcase their relevance in these areas

[367] Meghalaya: The State continues to remain peaceful with dwindling support base for Garo National Liberation Army (GNLA

[368] The violence perpetrated by the GNLA remained largely confined to Garo hills

[369] Spillover of the activities of terrorist groups was also visible in neighbouring districts of Goalpara and Dhubri in Assam

[370] The State Assembly elections were conducted peacefully in February

[371] Mizoram: The State continued to remain peaceful

[372] However, there were an increase in attempts by insurgent groups to smuggle arms and narcotics

[373] Due to the ongoing counter-insurgency operations by Myanmar Army against Myanmar Ethnic Armed Groups (EAG) along the tri-junction of India, Myanmar and Bangladesh, a spillover of EAG activities and influx of Myanmar population fearing violence by EAGs were observed in South Mizoram

[374] Proactive measures are thus being taken to establish a coordinated intelligence grid and undertake effective border management to preclude any deterioration of situation on our side of India-Myanmar Border

[375] Tripura: The State has remained comparatively peaceful and violence was within the threshold of law and order domain

[376] The year 2018 witnessed reduced levels of violence which reflect the efforts of the Security Forces to ensure transition of security environment from volatility to peace and tranquility

[377] The region is at the cusp of major changes and large infrastructure and communication projects are on the anvil as part of ‘Act East Policy’

[378] The ongoing NRC update and Naga Peace Accord is likely to have a pan-regional impact and situation needs to be proactively monitored in the coming months

[379] Left Wing Extremism (LWE): Anti LWE operations are being conducted by State Governments and MHA

[380] Army is involved only in advisory capacity and is providing training to the State Police/ CAPFs including training for Counter Improvised Explosive Devices Operations

[381] Nominated young officers from CAPF units are attached with Army battalions deployed in J&K and in the North East Region with the aim of grooming them for leading their sub units in Anti LWE operations & by giving them ‘operational exposure’ and ‘hands-on training’

[382] Situation Along the India-China Border 3.29 The situation along the India-China border has remained peaceful

[383] There are few areas along the border where there are differing perceptions of the LAC

[384] Both sides patrol upto their respective perceptions of LAC

[385] Specific cases of transgression by Chinese patrols into such areas are taken up with Chinese Authorities through the established mechanism of Hotlines, Border Personnel and Flag Meetings

[386] Compared to last year, the number of transgressions this year have considerably reduced

[387] Concomitantly, the percentage of Face Offs/ Aggressive Interactions during these transgressions has also reduced this year

[388] Post the Wuhan Summits, there has been an increase in the numbers of Flag Meetings

[389] This may be attributed to intent to resolve outstanding issues through discussion at various levels

[390] Standoff at CNN Junction, Eastern Ladakh due to our construction of a benign track and the constant raising of the construction of our Temporary Operating Base at Andrathang, Arunachal Pradesh were the only instances where there was major difference of opinion between the two sides

[391] A few Confidence Building Measures (CBMs) which had been proposed by both sides for consideration have been implemented in sensitive areas of Arunachal Pradesh thereby easing the tension to some extent

[392] Some additional CBMs are under consideration by both sides

[393] Situation in Doklam Plateau: Post the disengagement on August 28, 2017, after the 72 days standoff at Doklam, troops of both sides have redeployed themselves away from their respective positions near the face off site

[394] The strength of either side has, however, reduced

[395] The Indian Army is continuously monitoring Chinese activities in the area and is adequately prepared to respond to any contingency

[397] It is pertinent to note that the previous such incoming visit by the Chinese Defence Minister was in September

[402] DEFENCE COOPERATION WITH FRIENDLY FOREIGN COUNTRIES Defence Cooperation activities constitute an important tool for furtherance of our national interests and foreign policy objectives

[403] In keeping with India’s rising global stature in recent years, there has been a considerable increase in Defence Cooperation activities undertaken by the Indian Army

[404] Accordingly, an increasing number of Friendly Foreign Countries (FFCs) have shown keen interest to engage with the Indian Army, which is viewed not only as the world’s second largest standing Army but also as a professional, apolitical force with extensive combat experience and exemplary training standards

[450] Indian Army’s modernisation strategy covers the entire spectrum of conflict

[451] Major initiatives have been undertaken at organisational and ministerial levels to provide impetus to acquisition and defence reforms

[452] During the Financial Year 2018-19, 13 contracts worth ₹ 8277.40 crore have been signed for capital procurement of defence equipment for Army such as Bullet Proof Jacket (BPJ), Guns, Short Span Bridge, Electronic Fuzes and Ammunition

[453] The key facts of modernisation pursuits for various Arms and Services are as follows: (a) Mechanised Forces: Emphasis is on increasing effectiveness index of existing fleet of Tanks and BMPs through night enablement, enhancing mobility and accuracy. (b) Infantry: Impetus is being given to augmenting survivability, mobility and close quarter battle capability for combat and special operations

[454] A major boost has been given to Infantry with the procurement of Bullet Proof Jackets and Assault Rifles. (c) Artillery

[455] Capability enhancement of Artillery is focused on acquiring long range firing platforms and increasing lethality, precision and surveillance capabilities

[456] Upgrades of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle systems, weaponisation of aerial platforms and induction of additional artillery guns

[457] Pinaka MLRS Weapon System (d) Army Air Defence

[458] Emphasis is being laid on upgrades of existing fleet, responsive air defence for Strike formations in plains and tactical air defence in mountains

[459] In addition, procurement/ upgrades of Air Defence Guns and equipment are at fairly advanced stages

[460] e) Army Aviation: Army Aviation is enhancing its firepower and surveillance capability

[461] The Army Aviation fleet will undergo a major transformation with induction of new helicopters including weaponised platforms which enhance the fighting capability. (f) Signals: Major impetus has been laid on Electronic Warfare equipment, achieving robust communication grid in high altitude area and end to end data encryption

[462] g) Engineers & Combat Logistics

[463] Emphasis has been laid on acquiring all-terrain mobility, versatile bridging equipment, family of mines and enhanced engineering support in mountains as well as for mechanised forces in plains / deserts

[464] A number of initiatives have been undertaken to streamline and hasten the procurement process keeping in view the provisions of Defence Procurement Procedure –

[465] The Government regularly monitors progress of ongoing procurement projects, so as to ensure that the Army is equipped to meet the entire spectrum of security challenges

[466] Alignment with ‘Make in India’: Indian Army’s capability development plans are aligned with the ‘Make in India’ initiative to commitment to Nation Building

[467] Of the 16 cases of Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) accorded to major Schemes in the current Financial Year, 10 Schemes are ‘Buy Indian (Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured)’, 4 are ‘Buy (Indian)’ and 1 Scheme is ‘Buy’ and ‘Make’ with ToT to OFB

[468] The Armed Forces have also been accorded enhanced financial powers to meet immediate requirements

[469] Army Design Bureau: The Army Design Bureau (ADB) in the Perspective Planning Directorate is spearheading the Indian Army’s initiative of supporting, developing and handholding of Indian Defence Industry so as to achieve self-reliance in defence equipment as part of ‘Make in India’ initiative of Government of India

[470] One of the major initiatives undertaken by the ADB was the publication of three Compendiums of Problem Definition Statements which identified the core issues of concern for the Indian Army

[471] ADB is also supporting development of technology through Army Technology Board (ATB), Technology Development Fund (TDF), Make-II and Innovation for Defence Excellence (iDEX

[472] In the year 2018, nine ATB projects, nine TDP projects, seventeen Make-II projects and three iDEX projects have been launched to support development of technologies which can provide solutions to Problem Statements

[473] Twenty two solutions provided by Industry are under examination by Field Formations at operational locations

[474] a) Ammunition Stocks: A number of major initiatives have been taken for improving ammunition stocks of Indian Army

[475] This multi-pronged strategy is going to result in gradual build-up of ammunition. (b) Ammunition Roll on Plan: The management of ammunition is done by placing five-year Roll on Indent on Ordnance Factory Board (OFB) to enable it to plan its production

[476] The indent is placed on mutually agreed targets keeping the OFB capacity in view

[477] The first five-year Roll on Indent for 2010 to 2014 was placed on OFB in February

[478] The second Roll on indent was placed on OFB in October 2013 for projected requirement of five-year perspective plan for year 2014 to

[479] Production reports of OFB are being monitored monthly and shortfalls are being highlighted

[480] c) Ammunition Road Map

[481] During mid-course evaluation of Five-Year Roll on Plan of ammunition, need was felt for preparing Ammunition Road Map to address the criticalities

[482] Ammunition Road Map was approved by Ministry of Defence to meet ammunition requirement

[483] The ammunition procurement plan approved under the Ammunition Road Map includes placing of additional requirements on OFB and procurement of some ammunition items ex-import. Emergency Procurement of Ammunition: Ministry of Defence delegated Emergency Procurement powers to VCOAS in October

[484] As a result of this delegation, done with a view to making up of critical deficiency of Indian Army, many contracts were finalized for various critical ammunition, armament, vehicles and spares items

[486] e) Delegation of Powers to Maintain Minimum Stock Level of Critical Ammunition and Spares

[545] India is a maritime nation and the country sits astride a large number of busy International Shipping Lanes that criss-cross the Indian Ocean

[546] About 90% of our trade by volume and 70% by value is transported over the seas

[547] For a rapidly growing economy seeking new markets worldwide, the volume of maritime trade will only grow in times to come

[548] India’s economic resurgence is directly linked to her overseas trade and energy needs, most of which are transported by sea

[549] Mercantile trade constitutes a substantial portion of India’s GDP and is likely to increase in the future

[550] Maintenance of a secure maritime environment which enables unhindered pursuit of economic activities is, therefore, essential for the overall economic development and security of the country

[551] The last decade has witnessed India’s dependence on her maritime environment expanding substantially as her economic, military and technological strength grew, her global interactions widened and her national security imperatives and political interests stretched gradually beyond the Indian Ocean Region

[552] It can thus be assumed that the 21st century will be the ‘Century of the Seas’ for India and that the oceans will remain a key enabler in her global resurgence

[553] The Indian Navy (IN) has been playing a maritime leadership role in the Indian Ocean Region due to its multi-dimensional capabilities and active presence in the region

[554] The environment in India’s maritime neighbourhood is dynamic with increased instabilities, deepening geopolitical and ethnic fault lines, growing military capabilities and wide range of security challenges

[555] These pose a combination of conventional and sub-conventional threats emanating to India, at and from the seas

[556] These threats and challenges require the Indian Navy to remain effective across the entire spectrum of combat operations and constantly reshape itself to meet future challenges

[557] The Indian Navy is the key enabler and guarantor of the country’s maritime sovereignty and myriad use-of-the-sea activities

[558] This is discharged by the Navy through its four roles – military, diplomatic, constabulary and benign

[559] The objective of the Navy’s military role is deterrence/ dissuasion against any intervention or act which is against our national interests, and the ability to inflict a crushing defeat on the adversary in the event of hostilities

[560] A major objective of the Navy’s Constabulary role is to ensure coastal and offshore security and implement anti-piracy measures in conjunction with the Coast Guard and other Central and State agencies

[561] A high degree of Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) is being maintained by utilising IN assets and resources

[562] The IN stands fully ready to respond to any contingency in an appropriate manner

[563] A new Mission-based deployment concept has been implemented

[564] Mission-ready ships and aircraft are being deployed in ‘pole-positions’ along critical sea lanes of communications and choke points

[565] The deployed assets are ready to meet any eventuality across the spectrum of operations

[566] One frontline Fleet ship has been continuously deployed in the Gulf of Aden region since October 2008 for anti-piracy operations and provides safe escort to merchant ships of Indian and foreign nationalities

[567] Protection to our offshore assets, including Offshore Development Areas (ODAs) is being ensured through deployment of Immediate Support Vessels (ISVs) and other assets

[568] Regular exercises have been conducted to validate the safety and security of ODA platforms, which are vital to India’s energy security

[569] The IN has been actively pursuing activities towards capability building and capacity enhancement of Navies of friendly countries in the IOR

[570] Towards this end, India has been providing hardware and platforms, which includes ships and aircraft, for Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) surveillance

[571] IN has also been instrumental in development of maritime infrastructure of friendly nations

[572] IN initiatives contribute towards developing operational and technical skills to friendly foreign countries

[573] A new Transition cycle that allows for a focused and gradual transition of ships from periods of maintenance layoffs to full-scale operations has been implemented

[574] The new Transition cycle focusses efforts of Operational Commanders on the training and safety inspections of ships prior to their deployment for operations

[575] This is enhancing both ‘Combat Readiness’ and ‘Safety Standards’ on board ships

[794] INDIAN COAST GUARD chapter 6 6.1 Indian Coast Guard (ICG) came into existence on February 1, 1977 with two frigates and five patrol boats transferred from the Indian Navy and was formally instituted on August

[795] Since its inception, the service has acquired a wide range of capabilities, both surface and airborne, to undertake the assigned tasks during peace time and to supplement the efforts of the Indian Navy

[796] Organisation: The Command and Control of Coast Guard organisation lies with the Director General Indian Coast Guard (DG, ICG), New Delhi

[797] The organization has 5 Regional Headquarters located at Gandhinagar, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata and Port Blair which have been further sub-divided into 16 Coast Guard Districts Headquarters covering the entire coastline of India

[798] There are 42 Coast Guard Stations, 10 Coast Guard Air Stations and Air Enclave for undertaking effective deployment of ships and airborne operations

[799] Duties and Functions: The duties and functions of Indian Coast Guard are as follows: (a) Ensuring the safety and protection of the artificial islands, offshore terminals, installation and other structures and devices in any maritime zone

[800] b) Provide protection to the fishermen including assistance to them at sea while in distress

[801] c) Taking such measures as are necessary to preserve and protect the Marine Environment and to prevent and control marine pollution

[802] d) Assisting the Customs and other authorities in Anti-Smuggling Operations

[803] e) Enforcing the provision of such enactments as are for the time being in force in the maritime zones; and (f) Such other matter, including measures for the safety of life and property at sea and collection of scientific data, as may be prescribed

[804] During the Course of time, Indian Coast Guard has been assigned the additional duties of enforcement, monitoring and surveillance of Deep Sea Fishing, Search and Rescue for mariners and Marine oil-spill response measures

[805] ICG also provides coastal security in territorial waters in coordination with central and state agencies and it is the Lead Intelligence Agency for coastal and sea borders

[806] Existing Force Level: At present, Indian Coast Guard is equipped with 62 ships, 61 Interceptor Boats, 18 hovercrafts and 63 aircrafts

[863] Achievements of Indian Coast Guard S. No. Achievements during the period January, 2018 to March, 2019 (a) Search and Rescue (SAR) Mission 253 (b) Search and Rescue (SAR) Sortie 368 (c) Lives Saved at Sea 801 (d) Medical Evacuation at Sea 45 (e) Poaching Trawler Apprehension 10 Boats, 53 Crew (f) Repatriation of fishermen 174 Indian Fishermen from Sri Lanka 11 Sri Lankan fishermen from India 26 Pakistani fishermen from India 7.1 The Department of Defence Production (DDP) was set up in November 1962 with the objective of developing a comprehensive production infrastructure to produce the weapons/systems/platforms/equipment required for defence

[864] Over the years, the Department has established wide ranging production facilities for various defence equipment through the Ordnance Factories, Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) and private defence industry

[865] The products being manufactured by these units include arms and ammunition, tanks, armoured vehicles, heavy vehicles, fighter aircraft and helicopters, warships, submarines, missiles, ammunition, electronic equipment, earth moving equipment, special alloys and special purpose steels

[866] Department also recognizes that true self-reliance is only possible when the technology is also with the country

[867] Therefore, the Department has been encouraging promotion of innovation and Intellectual Property creation in the defence industry ecosystem of the country

[868] As a result of the efforts taken to develop defence production ecosystem, the country has achieved capability in wide range of defence and aerospace

[869] As far as land systems are concerned, these include Artillery guns, tanks, various types of heavy vehicles, mine protected vehicles, various kinds of small arms, armoured material including bulletproof jackets and helmets, wide range of ammunition, propellants and explosives, etc

[870] As regards aerosystems, fourth generation fighter aircrafts, helicopters of 3-5.5 tonne class, trainer aircrafts, missiles of several types, and as regards naval systems are concerned, capability to manufacture practically all type of naval vessels including offshore patrol vessels, corvettes, frigates, destroyers, aircraft carriers, submarines etc. has been created in the country

[871] Growth in Value of Production by Defence PSUs: With the objective of achieving self-reliance in defence and making India a global hub in defence manufacturing, the defence industry ecosystem has enhanced, their capabilities upgraded and product range widened

[872] A number of major products have been developed through research and development initiatives in addition to a number of products and equipment being produced through transfer of technology

[873] As a result of these efforts, increase in Value of Production (VoP) of Defence PSUs is indicated in the following figures

[874] Although figures of value of production are not readily available, as several industries are in delicensed category, similar growth in value of production is also projected for private industry

[875] Ordnance Factories have shown slight decline in the value of production as 275 items earlier reserved for Ordnance factories have been notified for open industry procurement

[876] Several Defence PSUs have recorded their highest-ever turnover during

[877] Details in this regard are as follows: Defence PSU Turnover during 2018-19 HAL 19705 crore BEL 11780 crore MDL 4550 crore BEML 3450 crore

[878] In order to redefine the role and functioning of CPSEs in the context of Vision-2022, Department of Public Enterprises organized CPSE Conclave on April

[879] Prime Minister had posed five specific challenges to the CPSEs and directed all the CPSEs to prepare action plans to achieve the targets emanating from recommendations of CPSE Conclave

[880] In follow-up of first challenge, i.e. Maximizing Geo-Strategic reach of Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs), it is proposed that 25% of Annual Turnover of respective DPSUs should be from Export by 2022-23 so that India becomes a significant exporter instead of being a mere importer

[881] The second challenge which the DPSUs have to achieve relates to reduction in their import dependence for components and parts used by them in production of various platforms and equipment

[882] Import substitution amounting to 15,000 crore by 2022-23 through indigenization of products/process is targeted as part of this effort

[883] With regard to developing capability and capacity in latest technologies, the third challenge is that the DPSUs have been asked to develop a roadmap for developing Artificial Intelligence based technologies for their platforms/equipment and implement the same

[884] Defence Exports: Over one dozen reforms / steps taken during 2018-19 which have provided a big boost to defence exports in the country

[885] As a result, the authorisations for defence exports in the country have seen quantum jump in the last two years

[886] The defence export authorizations have touched 10,745 crore during 2018-19, a growth of over 100% over 2017-18 when the authorizations were 4,682 crore and over 800% since 2016-17 when the defence authorizations were 1521 crore

[887] Further, due to several measures to enhance ease of doing business in exports by reforming export permission processes and developing a completely end-to-end online portal for receiving and processing authorization permissions, the time taken for authorization has reduced to less than 50% of time taken in

[888] New export offices have been opened by Defence PSU BEL

[889] BEL opened an Export Office in Hanoi, Vietnam, on June 13, 2018 and another Export office in Myanmar

[890] This exponential growth is a notable success of “Make in India in defence” and gives confidence that the country is moving towards becoming a net exporter of defence equipment / platforms after being one of world’s biggest importers of defence equipment for decades

[891] Some of the policy initiatives, reforms/steps taken in this regard are mentioned as below: (a) Special Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies (SCOMET) Category 6 titled “Munitions List” that was hitherto “Reserved” has been populated and Military Stores list notified vide Notification No. 115(RE-2013)/2009-2014 dated March 13, 2015 stands rescinded. (b) The Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for issue of Export Authorisation for export of Munitions List has been revised and published on the website

[892] Consultation process has been done away with in repeat orders of same product to the same entity and export of items for exhibition purposes

[893] Legitimate export of the parts and components of small arms and body armour for civil use being permitted in consultation with MEA, Powers have been delegated to DRDO, DGOF, and CMD’s of DPSUs for exploring export opportunities and participation in global tenders

[894] In Intra-Company business the requirement of getting End User Certificate (EUC) from the Government of importing country has been done away with and ‘Buying’ Company is authorized to issue the EUC and a new provision for importing and re-exporting parts and components for undertaking repair or rework to provide replacement for a component under warranty obligation is inserted in the SOP as a sub-classification of repeat orders

[895] c) The existing online application system of export authorisation made more user-friendly

[896] New Online system for processing of export authorization applications launched

[897] The entire process made paperless right from filing of application by the industry to issue to export authorisation, including consultation with stakeholders

[898] d) MHA vide Notification dated November 1, 2018 delegated its powers to Department of Defence Production for issue of export license under Arms Rules 2016 in Form X-A, for parts and components of small arms to ensure that Department of Defence Production remains a single point of contact for exporters

[899] e) Scheme for Promotion of Defence Exports notified to provide an opportunity to the prospective exporters an option to get their product certified by the Government and access to the testing infrastructure of Ministry of Defence for initial validation of the product and its subsequent field trials

[900] The certificate can be produced by the prospective exporter for marketing their products suitably in the global market

[901] Standard Operating Procedure for implementation of the scheme has been notified and published on the website

[902] Export Promotion Cell: This cell is formed to co-ordinate and follow-up on export related action including enquiries received from various countries and facilitate private sector and public sector companies for export promotion

[903] DPSUs and OFB have been directed to have at least 25 percent as export target from out of their total sales

[904] Defence Attaches have also been mandated to provide support for defence export promotion

[905] An Export Booklet has also been published in which products of DPSUs/OFB and private companies dealing in manufacturing of defence products have been included

[907] Defence Industrial Corridors: Finance Minister in his Budget Speech on February 1, 2018 announced setting up of two Defence Corridors in the Country

[908] Consequently, it has been decided to develop one such corridor in Uttar Pradesh and the other one in Tamil Nadu

[909] While not restricting the growth of defence industry in any location, the five nodal points in Tamil Nadu and six nodal points in Uttar Pradesh with potential to develop defence industries in the corridor are indicated below

[910] a) Uttar Pradesh: Agra, Aligarh, Chitrakoot, Jhansi, Kanpur and Lucknow

[911] b) Tamil Nadu: Chennai, Coimbatore, Hosur, Salem, and Tiruchirappalli

[912] To elicit the views of the stake-holders in the vicinity of these areas, five Industry Interactions in Uttar Pradesh and six industry interactions in Tamil Nadu were organized

[913] Based on these consultations, on August 11, 2018, investments of over 3700 crore were announced for UP Corridor in an event held in Aligarh

[914] In a similar event held in Trichurapalli, Tamil Nadu on January 20, 2019, investments of over 3100 crore were announced for Tamil Nadu Defence corridor

[915] A Committee under chairmanship of Additional Secretary, DDP has been formed to monitor the implementation of these projects announced for the two corridors

[916] Additionally, a Joint Venture between OFB and Kalashnikov, Russia along with Rosonboron Export (ROE), Russia has also been approved in Korwa, UP for manufacture of AK-203 rifles and is expected to bolster the UP corridor

[917] Similarly, Defence Innovation Hub has been approved for Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu and is being developed with Coimbatore District Small Industries Association (CODISSIA) and is expected to provide a boost to Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial corridor

[918] Creating a Startup Ecosystem for Defence and Aerospace: Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) is a scheme formulated in collaboration with Startup India and Atal Innovation Mission, with the objective of bringing Start-ups to innovate, develop technology and solve problems related to defence and aerospace

[919] iDEX, a first initiative of its kind in the country, was launched by the Prime Minister on April

[920] iDEX is aimed at creation of an ecosystem to foster innovation and technology development in Defence and Aerospace by engaging Industries including SMEs, Start-ups, Individual Innovators, R&D institutes and Academia and provide them grants/funding and other support to carry out R&D

[921] It is expected that India can take advantage of its vibrant startup ecosystem to develop technologies related to defence and aerospace

[922] Under the iDEX scheme, Defence India Startup Challenges (DISCs) are being organized

[923] DISC comprises of real-life problems statements identified by Indian forces/Defence PSUs/OFB and thrown to the Startups to respond

[924] In the very first year of its existence, iDEX has organized two rounds of DISC challenges

[925] DISC-1, organized in August 2018, comprised of 11 challenges

[926] DISC-2 organized in January 2019 involved 4 challenges

[927] Working through partner incubators, iDEX has been able to galvanize a big startup community to take interest in problems floated under DISC challenges

[928] Over 600 responses have been received for the problems offered under DISC

[929] The status of DISC responses relating to the three Services are as follows

[930] Service No. of Challenges No. of Startup responses Indian Army 4 159 Indian Air Force 5 222 Indian Navy 4 173 HAL 2 82 Total 15 636 Under the iDEX scheme, a maximum of 1.5 crore funding is available to a participant for development of a prototype based on a college led by respective Service

[931] The selection is competitive and financial amount is released based on achievement of certain milestones

[932] The scheme provides for elimination based development wherein for each development, multiple participants are selected and at each milestone, some of the participants are dropped based on progress/performance

[933] iDEX is being implemented by Defence Innovation Organization, a SPV floated for this purpose with 50 crore support each from BEL and HAL

[934] Other Defence PSUs have also been asked to fund DIO

[935] A Special Purpose Vehicle, namely Defence Innovation Organization, was floated as a section 8 company, with equity of 50 crore each from Bharat Electronics Ltd. and Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd

[936] Subsequently, all Defence PSUs have been requested to contribute another 100 crore to the DIO

[937] A Memorandum of Intent (MoI) between iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) and DIU (Defence Innovation Unit), USA was signed on September

[938] This MoU will enable Indian Start Ups in Defence to have greater exposure to similar initiative being implemented in USA

Chandrasekaran, Chairman, Tata Sons to study the strategic implications of Artificial Intelligence in National Security and Defence needs and to make appropriate recommendations in this regard

[941] Establish a high level Defence AI Council (DAIC) headed by the Raksha Mantri, with the three Service Chiefs, Defence Secretary, Secretary (DP), Secretary (DRDO), FA(DS), National Cyber Security Coordinator, CISC, representatives from industry and academia as its members

[963] During the year, DDP has initiated a new programme to promote greater culture of innovation and technology development in Defence PSUs and OFB

[964] As part of this effort, “Mission Raksha Gyanshakti” programme was started targeting to train DPSU and OFB employees and to file greater number of patents for new technologies/process innovations made by them

[965] This Mission was launched formally by Raksha Mantri on November

[968] Other Major Initiatives: Several Initiatives have been taken by Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence to promote defence production in the country

[969] Some of the salient initiatives are mentioned below: (a) Revised Make-II procedure: A Revised Make-II procedure was approved by Government in February 2018 to enable greater participation of industry in defence supply of capital items

[970] The salient features of the new Make-II procedure include the following: (i) There will be no limit to the number of industry who may respond to the Expression of Interest (EoI) for development of the prototype subject to meeting the minimum qualification criteria

[971] ii) Once the RFP is issued, it shall not be retracted

[972] The industry who wins the bid, is assured of an order

[973] The case will be progressed even if there is single entity offering an innovative solution

[974] iv) Normally, there shall be no negotiations by Contract Negotiation Committee (CNC) in multi-vendor contracts

[975] v) It aims to reduce time from in-principle approval to placing of order by 50%

[976] Upto December 31, 2018, 34 Make-II projects had been granted Approval-in-Principle

[977] These include 14 projects for Indian Army, 9 projects for Indian Airforce and 11 projects for the Indian Navy. Suo-Moto proposals: Under the Revised Make-II, a new feature has been introduced which enables industry to make proposals to the Services for their use

[978] A Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for consideration of ‘suo-moto’ proposals of Capital Acquisition has been issued in June

[979] The Services examine the proposal and if they find it relevant to their needs, they can take its development under the Make-II procedure

[980] This suo-moto proposal is novel and for the first time enables industry to initiate proposals for use of the Services

[981] The suo-moto has particular relevance for new technologies/new products being developed by start-ups/industry

[982] The suo-moto proposals can be submitted online through website makeinindiadefence.gov.in

[983] Till December 31, 2018, 4 proposals have been granted Approval-in-Principle and 41 proposals are consideration of the three Services. (c) Indigenization Policy: A new Policy for Indigenization of components & spares in defence platforms for DPSUs and OFB has been notified on March

[984] The Indigenization Policy is a set of strategies for indigenization of components & spares in defence platforms

[985] The objective of the policy is “to create an industry ecosystem which is able to indigenize the imported components (including alloys & special materials) and sub-assemblies for defence equipment and platform manufactured in India and to leverage the said capability to create components export market”

[986] It is estimated that Defence PSUs will reduce the import bill more than ₹ 15000 crore by 2022 through indigenization of products and processes

[987] d) Streamlining Industrial Licensing

[988] Based on the initiative taken by Department of Defence Production the following liberalisation has been done in licensing of items covered under Arms Act:  MHA vide notification dated November 1, 2018, had notified Arms Rules 2016 (Third Amendment) wherein it has notified that Firearms (Small Arms and ammunitions and allied items of caliber upto 12.7 mm) and their following parts only are licensable under Arms Act, 1959/Arms Rules

[989] a. Barrel b. Cylinder c. Bolt d. Breach block e. Slide f. Firing Pin g. Frame or Receiver h. Extractor i. Hammer/Striker

[990] Further, MHA vide notification dated December 14, 2018 in supersession of their earlier notification S.O. 1636(E) dated May 19, 2017 had revised the schedule of items requiring Industrial License (IL) under delegated powers to Secretary(DIPP) under Arms Act/Arms Rule according to which “Tanks and other armoured fighting vehicles” and “Arms and ammunitions and allied items of defence equipment; other than small arms of calibre 12.7 mm and above” are only licensable under Arms Act, 1959/Arms Rules 2016”

[991] There has been steady increase in the number of Industrial Licenses issued for defence manufacturing

[992] Government has issued 439 ILs till March 2019 for manufacture of a wide range of defence items to private companies

[993] This is almost double the number of licenses that existed in March

[994] The bar chart indicating Industrial Licenses issued during last three years is as shown below

[995] In May 2001, the defence industry sector, which was hitherto reserved for the public sector, was opened up to 100% for Indian private sector participation with Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) up to 26%, both subject to licensing

[996] However, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce & Industry vide Press Note No. 5 (2016 Series), has allowed FDI under automatic route upto 49% and above 49% through Government route wherever it is likely to result in access to modern technology or for other reasons to be recorded

[997] Further, defence industry is subjected to IL under Industries (Development & Regulation) Act, 1951 and manufacturing of small arms and ammunitions under the Arms Act, 1959/Arms Rules

[998] So far 42 FDI proposal / Joint Ventures have been approved in defence sector for manufacture of various defence equipments

[999] Further, significant FDI inflows in Defence and Aerospace sectors have been witnessed

[1028] Software Defined Radio is a basic device which is required for all communications by forces and is set to replace the traditional radio systems

[1029] A committee was constituted on November 8, 2018 under the chairmanship of Dr Abhay Karandikar, Director IIT Kanpur for preparing a roadmap for development of Indigenous Software Defined Radio (SDR) ecosystem with a focus to meet requirements of strategic sector and Defence Service indigenously

[1031] Based on their recommendations, the following major decisions have been taken

[1032] A Defence Standard Authority to be set up under Directorate of Standardisation, which will consist of all stakeholders including Academia, Services, DRDO and industry

[1033] This Authority will undertake all activities to prepare and maintain Indian SDR/SCA standards, develop and hold a repository of common waveform, manage issues related to testing and certifications in due course

[1034] ii) Decision to source SDRs from indigenous sources

[1035] In accordance with above decisions, a Standards Development Authority (SDA) has been constituted on March 7, 2019 under Directorate of Standardisation (DoS/DDP) towards development/preparation of standards for critical/emerging technologies which have defence & strategic sector applicability and are critical for self-reliance

[1036] As part of their initial work, technical work for developing standards for Software Defined Radio (SDR) has been initiated by SDA under Chairmanship of Dr. Abhay Karandikar, Director IIT Kanpur

[1390] The organisation has set its sights on making India self-sufficient in Defence equipments ranging from missiles, radars, sonars, electronic warfare, engineering systems, surveillance and recce systems, communication systems, electro-optics, night vision, information security products to name a few

[1391] At the core of its technological strength is its expertise in system design, system integration and testing & evaluation built over the last six decades

[1392] DRDO’s mission essentially covers the following broad activities: • Design, develop and lead to production of state-of-the-art sensors, weapon systems, platforms and allied equipment for our Defence Services

[1393] Provide technological solutions to the Services to optimize combat effectiveness and to promote well-being of the troops. • Develop infrastructure and committed quality manpower and build strong indigenous technology base. •

[1394] Support National Cyber Security Architecture – Testing capabilities, security solutions, hardware testing, indigenous network systems, cyber defence tools 8.3 DRDO’s major achievements were made possible by working in close synchronization with all its major partners which include tri-Services, industries and academia

[1395] Today over 1000 industries including Defence Public Sector Undertaking (DPSUs) and Ordnance Factory Board (OFBs) are vital partners in DRDO’s development programmes

[1396] In addition, DRDO collaborates with other S&T organisations like Department of Space (DoS), Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) and Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) for common requirements and applications

[1397] DRDO has also selectively chosen its global partners and has MoUs signed with over 30 countries worldwide for joint collaboration in requisite areas with complementary work share

[1398] DRDO Partners and Linkages are reflected in the chart below: 8.4 DRDO is headed by Secretary DD R&D & Chairman DRDO

[1399] Dr. G. Satheesh Reddy has taken over charge as Secretary, Defence R&D, Chairman, DRDO in August

[1401] There are five corporate DGs to oversee the activities of the corporate HQ
