[4350] Defence Work Procedure (DWP) - 2007 stipulates that Revised Administrative Approval (RAA) will be essential before tender if there is change in the scope of work due to any reason, irrespective of whether the cost is within the tolerance limit of 10 per cent or not

[4351] MoD, in March 2011, sanctioned for construction of a Baffle Range at Indian Military Academy (IMA), Dehradun for firing training

[4352] The work was awarded in December 2012 for ₹ 8.66 crore for completion by February

[4353] The tender included drawing for staggered fashion boundary wall but the quantities of the materials for the wall, originally based on straight boundary wall, were erroneously not amended

[4354] Within a day of conclusion of the contract, the process for RAA was initiated to incorporate deviations

[4355] Thereafter the matter remained under correspondence between various authorities and the work was held up for want of approval of the RAA and the assets created were lying unused as of July

[4356] As of March 2017, the physical progress of the work was 91 percent and expenditure of ₹ 7.60 crore had been incurred

[4357] Loss of ₹ 56.17 lakh besides avoidable liability of ₹ 9.27 crore Ministry of Defence (Ministry) accorded a sanction in March 2003 for construction of accommodation for Infantry Battalion at Suratgarh at a cost of ₹ 4.86 crore

[4358] The main scope of work catered for construction of total 36 structures which included living accommodation, officer mess, storage accommodation, garages etc

[4359] However, poor workmanship and inadequate monitoring during execution of work at Suratgarh led to construction of unsafe and substandard buildings thereby warranting their demolition and subsequent reconstruction/ rehabilitation at total estimated cost of ₹ 9.83 crore just after seven years of construction

[4360] Delay in provisioning of air-conditioners denied the ready availability of Missiles to a field formation. Storage accommodation for Missile constructed at a cost of ` 2.20 crore in 2008 could not be put to the desired use due to non-availability of air conditioners

[4361] Despite the user requirement, the initiative for provisioning of air conditioners was inordinately delayed and thereby the Field Formation was functioning without holding of Missiles in its Armoury

[4362] Given the mountainous terrain, hostile weather conditions and the fact that the area remains cut off from the mainland for more than six months in a year, stocking of the critical ammunition like Missiles at a distant location under inhospitable geographical conditions impairs the operational readiness of the field formation

[4363] Paragraph 4.3) Engineer Stores of Engineer Origin-Follow up Audit Engineer Regiments provide critical mobility support to the armed forces both in war and peace times

[4364] Our review, however, indicates persistence of some chronic issues which, if not addressed, will continue to pose serious challenge to this critical support system for the armed forces

[4365] Some of these issues are shortages of stores and spares across the categories, accentuated by delays and inefficiencies in the procurement system that results in an unduly long procurement cycle and consequently the inability to spend the allocated funds

[4366] Lack of an automated system created bottlenecks in the two-way flow of information across different parts of the organization and led to inadequate control and monitoring

[4367] This resulted in delays in registration of demands for stores and their eventual issue, uneven distribution of stores, and also infructuous expenditure in purchases of unwarranted spares

[4368] The delay in initiation approval of PRCs and the inability to finalize the purchase proposals in time aggravated the availability of plants and spares

[4369] Non-formulation of five year perspective roll-on plans for repairs and delays in finalization of annual targets delayed provisioning of stores and spares

[4370] The non-compliance with the overhaul policy led to a situation where the equipment and plants were pressed into service without the scheduled overhauls, potentially impacting their optimum performance

[4371] In order to address some of the issues mentioned above, MoD should inter alia: Consider on-boarding the ESD onto its Computerised Inventory Control Project being rolled out in the Directorate General of Ordnance Services, which deals with inventory management of ordnance stores

[4372] Strictly enforce the existing provisions for mid-life overhaul of plants and equipment in order to ensure that their performance is optimal

[4373] Streamline the purchase process to make it accountable and result-oriented

[4374] Fix the periodicity of the meetings of the purchase committee and make it mandatory for the members to attend it

[4375] Unfruitful expenditure Non-adherence to laid down Technical Instructions of Director General of Border Roads (DGBR) regarding work of realignment/construction of roads led to foreclosure of work resulting in unfruitful expenditure of 15.58 crore in two cases given below

[4376] As per the technical instructions, the hill roads should be constructed much ahead of the construction of permanent bridges

[4377] Two sanctions were accorded in 2011 by Director General of Border Roads (DGBR) for improvement of a road and construction of a bridge on ‘Y-Z’ road in State ‘V’ to facilitate movement of artillery gun carrying vehicle

[4378] The bridge work commenced in May 2012 without completing the work of improving the zigs and curves on this road

[4379] Border Roads Organization (BRO) in October 2015 initiated foreclosure of the bridge work after expenditure of ₹ 2.27 crore on the ground that it was not required in view of the approval of new alignment of the connecting road, thus, an expenditure of ₹ 2.27 crore became infructuous

[4380] Sanction was accorded in December, 2010 for construction of a Double lane for re-alignment of a 7 km stretch on National Highway 31 A to avoid major trouble at Mile 27 with problem of sinking area

[4381] No consultant/geologist, however, was involved in joint survey before commencement of the work

[4382] The work commenced in January, 2012 but during May-August 2013, a large number of slides/ slips took place resulting in huge damages of the executed works

[4383] In December, 2014, DGBR proposed to re-survey the alignment & appoint a consultant alongwith a geologist to prepare a Revised Details Project Report

[4384] As of October 2015, the physical progress of the work was 9.36 percent with expenditure of ₹ 9.13 crore

[4385] In addition, ₹ 1.14 crore had been paid for compensatory afforestation and ₹ 2.77 crore for land use for the road

[4386] In August, 2015, DGBR recommended termination of contract

[4387] Thus, expenditure of ₹ 13.31 crore did not serve the intended purpose

[4388] Chapter VI: Defence Research and Development Organization Loss due to inadequate terms of insurance for imported equipment Instruments Research & Development Establishment (IRDE), placed a supply order on a foreign firm in August 2012 for purchase of an imported polishing machine at a cost of ` 19.68 crore and contracted M/s Balmer Lawrie for shipment of the equipment from England to India

[4389] The insurance policy purchased by Balmer Lawrie from Oriental Insurance Company covered the risk of deferred unpacking upto 30 days

[4390] The consignment was opened after nearly 3 months and the machine was found beyond economic repairs

[4391] The Insurance Surveyor rejected the claim stating that the policy included insurance cover for 30 days period for deferred unpacking only

[4392] Action had been initiated to recover the damages from Balmer Lawrie but there was no outcome as of February

[4393] It is recommended that the Procurement Manual procedure should be suitably amended to incorporate clear responsibility for ensuring that high value equipment is covered by an appropriate insurance policy, for monitoring the factors that are critical for insurance claims and for ensuring that those factors are monitored at the appropriate level

[4394] Paragraph 6.1) Avoidable Procurement of stores valuing ₹ 6.09 crore for stockpiling As per general principles of purchase in the Purchase Management Manual, 2006 of Defence Research & Development Organization (DRDO), all expenditure on purchases will only be need based and stores should not be procured to stockpile in anticipation of future requirements

[4395] In two cases, Combat Vehicle Research & Development Establishment procured stores valuing ₹ 6.09 crore for stockpiling citing future utilization

[4396] The stores are still held in stock

[4397] The stockpiling not only resulted in blocking of government money, but its future utilization is also uncertain

[4398] Unfruitful expenditure of ₹ 13.78 crore in taking up a project without complete test facilities Defence Research & Development Organization (DRDO) takes up various types of projects for research and development

[4399] Test and Evaluation is a continuous process during the development of a system

[4400] The availability of test facilities is, therefore, of paramount importance for taking up a project

[4401] Research and Development Establishment (Engineers

[4402] R&DE(E)], took up project for Aircraft Arrester Gear (AAG) required to arrest fighter aircraft 6-40 Ton capacity

[4403] The project was closed after incurring expenditure of ₹ 11.88 crore, without testing the AAG for its capability, as the adequate testing facilities were not available within the Country, a fact known to R&DE(E) even before taking up the project

[4404] Thereafter, it also constructed part test facility at a cost of Rs. 1.90 crore, despite knowing that the facility was inadequate to test the AAG at full load capacity and such testing was also hazardous for safety of personnel and infrastructure in the surrounding area

[4405] As the AAG could not be tested for 40 Ton load capacity, Centre for Military Airworthiness and Certification (CEMILAC) did not certify the AAG system for use by the Indian Air Force. Annual Report

[4406] Resultantly, the entire expenditure of ₹ 13.78 crore proved unfruitful
